definitions.explanation: The impulsive energy and lack of restraint characteristic of young people. Almost always appears in the fixed expression 若気の至り (a youthful indiscretion).

examples.japanese: {若気|わかげ}の{至|いた}りだった。
あれは{若気|わかげ}の{至|いた}りで、{今|いま}では{後悔|こうかい}している。
examples.english: That was a youthful indiscretion, and I regret it now.

examples.japanese: {若気|わかげ}の{至|いた}りとはいえ、{取|と}り{返|かえ}しのつかないことをしてしまった。
examples.english: Even though it was the recklessness of youth, I did something that can't be undone.

notes:
USAGE:
Almost exclusively used in the set phrase {若気|わかげ}の{至|いた}り (youthful indiscretion, literally "the culmination of youthful impetuousness"). This expression is used when looking back on something reckless or foolish done in one's youth. It carries a tone of self-deprecation or rueful reflection.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {若気|わかげ}の{至|いた}り (youthful indiscretion — the primary usage)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {血気|けっき}: hot-bloodedness — youthful reckless energy, as in {血気|けっき}にはやる (to act rashly out of youthful ardor)
- {青|あお}い: immature, green — describes someone who lacks experience
